steps.title: Prepare Grace's medium
steps.instruction: Add one bottle of Grace's medium powder and 0.35 g NaHCO₃ to 900 mL sterile distilled water, stir to dissolve, adjust pH to 6.5 with 1 M NaOH at room temperature, bring volume to 1 L with sterile water, filter through a 0.22 µm filter, dispense into 4.5 mL aliquots and store at 4 °C (stable for 4–5 months).

steps.title: Add supplements to culture medium
steps.instruction: To each 4.5 mL aliquot of Grace's medium add 250 µL fetal bovine serum, 200 µL sterile distilled water, 50 µL penicillin‑streptomycin, and 5 µL of 0.01 mg/mL 20‑Hydroxyecdysone (final concentration 20 nM). The extra 200 µL water balances osmotic pressure; the 5 µL 20‑Hydroxyecdysone is critical for early‑ and mid‑third‑instar disc cultivation.

steps.title: Coat dishes with Poly‑D‑Lysine
steps.instruction: Add 600 µL of 0.1 mg/mL Poly‑D‑Lysine to the centre of each glass‑bottom microwell dish, incubate overnight at 4 °C, remove surplus solution the next day, and dry the dish in a hood for 1 h (remove as much liquid as possible to avoid crystal formation).

steps.title: Select fly stocks for labeling
steps.instruction: Choose appropriate Drosophila stocks for the desired fluorescent markers (e.g., hsp‑flp; Act5C>CD2>Gal4 combined with UAS‑CD8‑GFP for membrane labeling, UAS‑RFP for cytoplasm, UAS‑Lifeact‑GFP for F‑actin, UAS‑His‑RFP for nuclei, Indy‑GFP for cell outlines, DE‑cad::mTomato for adherens junctions).

steps.title: Cross flies to generate fluorescent clones
steps.instruction: Cross virgin females of genotype hsp‑flp; Act5C>CD2>Gal4 with males carrying the chosen UAS‑fluorescent marker, raise the crosses in standard food vials for 5–7 days, changing vials every 2–3 days. Adults should be 5–7 days old before egg collection.

steps.title: Stage larvae and collect eggs
steps.instruction: Transfer 30–50 adult flies (≈70 % females, 30 % males) to a cage with an apple‑juice agar plate, keep overnight at 25 °C, discard the plate, then renew the plate with yeast every 2 h for 1 day. After 1 day, collect the plate, remove yeast, add fresh fly food to the centre, lid the plate and incubate at 25 °C for another day, then transfer larvae to a food vial.

steps.title: Induce clones by heat shock
steps.instruction: At 72–84 h after egg lay (AEL) subject larvae to a 10‑min heat shock at 37 °C in a water bath (ensure the entire food region containing larvae is submerged without water entering the vial), then incubate larvae at 25 °C. Dissect larvae 12–15 h after heat shock.

steps.title: Install CSBDeep and analysis software
steps.instruction: In Fiji, install the CSBDeep plugin from the update site. On the computer, install a compatible graphics card, Python, TensorFlow, and Jupyter Notebook (see https://github.com/CSBDeep/CSBDeep/tree/main/.github).

steps.title: Wash larvae and prepare culture droplets
steps.instruction: Float larvae out of food with distilled water, transfer each larva with forceps into a 60 mm sterile Petri dish containing 10 mL PBS, repeat washing in fresh PBS three times, prepare 15 droplets of culture medium (30 µL each) in the lid of a sterile Petri dish, give each larva one final wash in a droplet of culture medium (do not keep larvae in PBS >2 h).

steps.title: Dissect eye‑antennal imaginal discs
steps.instruction: Place a larva in a fresh droplet of culture medium, hold the body ~1/3 from the anterior with one pair of forceps, pull out the mouth hooks with a second pair, remove the attached eye‑antennal discs and brain, discard fat body and gut, transfer the discs‑brain complex to a new droplet, hold mouth hooks, use dissecting needles to separate brain from the discs, cut the discs off the mouth hooks, and finally transfer the isolated eye‑antennal discs to a fresh droplet with a 100 µL pipette.

steps.title: Dissect wing imaginal discs
steps.instruction: Place a larva in a fresh droplet of culture medium, cut the larva in half with two forceps preserving the anterior (mouth hooks), hold the mouth hooks and push the body wall inward to turn the larva inside‑out, remove brain, fat body, gut and other discs, cut the horizontal trachea between the two vertical tracheae with a dissecting needle, then cut the trachea connecting the notum tip of the wing disc to the body wall, and finally cut the trachea linking adult muscle precursors to the main vertical trachea; transfer the wing disc to a fresh droplet with a 100 µL pipette (frequently refresh droplets during dissection).

steps.title: Mount discs using cell culture insert
steps.instruction: Transfer each imaginal disc with ≤20 µL of culture medium onto a glass‑bottom microwell dish, flatten the droplet with the pipette, pull the disc to the edge of the droplet using the trachea (wing) or optic stalk (eye‑antennal) and orient apical‑up or basal‑up as needed, remove remaining medium to flatten the disc while leaving a thin residual film, cut the feet of a cell‑culture insert leaving ~40 µm spacer, place the insert on top of the disc, quickly add 200 µL culture medium into the insert (ensure no air bubbles; add more from the side if needed), seal the dish with its lid and parafilm.

steps.title: Mount discs on Poly‑D‑Lysine dishes
steps.instruction: Transfer each disc with ≤50 µL of culture medium onto a Poly‑D‑Lysine‑coated dish, gently flow medium around the disc with a dissecting needle to position apical‑up or basal‑up, remove excess medium with a pipette, quickly add 400 µL culture medium, and seal the dish with its lid and parafilm.

steps.title: Acquire live confocal images
steps.instruction: Place the 35 mm dish on the stage of an inverted confocal microscope, select lasers (e.g., 488 nm for GFP, 565 nm for RFP) and set power <5 %, set image size to 1024 × 700 px (or 1024 × 250 px for fast protein dynamics), adjust zoom to obtain 3.5–5.5 px/µm, define a z‑stack of 20–50 slices with 1.5 µm spacing, set acquisition interval to 5 or 10 min for up to 20 h (single stack acquisition 1–1.5 min), or for protein dynamics use 30–60 s intervals over 3 h, then start imaging.

steps.title: Generate training data for CSBDeep
steps.instruction: Prepare a dish with cultured imaginal discs expressing the same fluorophore as the experimental data, acquire 16‑bit image stacks using identical microscope settings as for raw data, record two channels simultaneously: Channel 1 with low laser power (as for raw images) and Channel 2 with high laser power (avoid over‑exposure), set z‑slice interval to 0.375 µm (¼ of the 1.5 µm raw interval), use frame‑scan mode with a black background, acquire at least five complete stacks per marker, then create a ‘data’ folder containing subfolders ‘low’ and ‘high’, split the two channels and save low‑power stacks in ‘low’ and high‑power stacks in ‘high’.

steps.title: Train CARE network model
steps.instruction: Download the unsampling‑3d workflow from https://github.com/CSBDeep/CSBDeep/tree/main/examples, copy the three notebooks (1_datagen.ipynb, 2_training.ipynb, 3_prediction.ipynb) into the marker folder (e.g., CD8‑GFP), open a terminal in that folder, start Jupyter Notebook (command ‘jupyter notebook’), run 1_datagen.ipynb (Shift‑Enter) to generate training files, then run 2_training.ipynb (≈1 h) to train the model; the trained model is saved as models/my_model/TF_SavedModel.zip.

steps.title: Denoise images with CSBDeep
steps.instruction: Load the 4‑D image stack into Fiji, apply Image → Scale → Z‑scale with factor 4, open Plugins → CSBDeep, select ‘Run network’, import the model file TF_SavedModel.zip, run the prediction to obtain a ‘result’ stack, reset brightness, convert the 32‑bit result to 8‑bit, and save the denoised stack (z‑resolution is ~4‑fold improved).
